claim: Axon caliber plays a crucial role in determining conduction velocity and, consequently, in the timing and synchronization of neural activation.
source: Axon caliber plays a crucial role in determining conduction velocity and, consequently, in the timing and synchronization of neural activation.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the relationship between axon caliber and conduction velocity.

claim: When confounding factors such as extra-axonal water and axonal orientation dispersion are eliminated, heavily diffusion-weighted MRI signals become sensitive to axon radii.
source: Here, we show how – when confounding factors such as extra-axonal water and axonal orientation dispersion are eliminated – heavily diffusion-weighted MRI signals become sensitive to axon radii.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Diffusion MRI is only capable of estimating a single metric, the effective radius, representing the entire axon radius distribution within a voxel that emphasizes the larger axons.
source: However, diffusion MRI is only capable of estimating a single metric, the effective radius, representing the entire axon radius distribution within a voxel that emphasizes the larger axons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from theoretical considerations and experimental observations in the study.

claim: The axon radius explains the largest proportion of variance in conduction velocity.
source: Using a model of action potential neurophysiology (Rushton, 1951), it has been shown that the axon radius explains the largest proportion of variance in conduction velocity (Drakesmith et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Smaller axons may be preferentially susceptible to axonal injury in multiple sclerosis.
source: For example, direct axon counting in post-mortem tissue has suggested that smaller axons may be preferentially susceptible to axonal injury in multiple sclerosis (Evangelou et al., 2001) due to inflammation (Campbell et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Electron microscopy has revealed a higher percentage of small-radius axons and a lower percentage of large-radius axons in several segments of the corpus callosum in autistic subjects compared to healthy controls.
source: Electron microscopy has revealed a higher percentage of small-radius axons and a lower percentage of large-radius axons in several anatomically and functionally distinct segments of the corpus callosum in autistic subjects compared to healthy controls (Wegiel et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to an electron microscopy study.

claim: Morphometric analysis of adult rat brains showed reduced axonal radii without axonal loss after chronic alcohol feeding.
source: From the animal literature, morphometric analysis of adult rat brains showed reduced axonal radii without axonal loss after chronic alcohol feeding (Kjellström and Conradi, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a morphometric analysis study.

claim: dMRI is sensitive to the thermal motion of water molecules and their interference with microscopic boundaries.
source: dMRI is sensitive to the thermal motion of water molecules and their interference with microscopic boundaries, such as imparted by cells and subcellular structures in the brain (Tanner, 1979; Le Bihan, 2003; Le Bihan et al., 1986; Callaghan et al., 1988; Basser et al., 1994; Jones, 2010; Beaulieu, 2002; Novikov et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge about dMRI, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Axon radius mapping using dMRI remains highly contested.
source: Several studies have used various methods to report on axon radius parameters; still, despite many attempts, axon radius mapping using dMRI remains highly contested (Assaf et al., 2013; Horowitz et al., 2015; Alexander et al., 2010; Innocenti et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2014; Burcaw et al., 2015; Ong et al., 2008; Ong and Wehrli, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies showing controversy in the field.

claim: Discrepancies between histology and dMRI-derived axon radii uncovered various confounding factors including orientation dispersion.
source: Discrepancies between histology and dMRI-derived axon radii uncovered various confounding factors, for example orientation dispersion (Drobnjak et al., 2016; Nilsson et al., 2012), time-dependent extra-axonal diffusion overshadowing the intra-axonal signal at low diffusion weighting (Burcaw et al., 2015; Fieremans et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2018), weak signal attenuation for typically very narrow axons, especially in the realistic experimental regime of long diffusion gradient duration (van Gelderen et al., 1994; Neuman, 1974), and/or putative shrinkage during tissue preparation (Barazany et al., 2009; Innocenti et al., 2015; Aboitiz et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies identifying confounding factors.

claim: dMRI can be made specific to a particular water population restricted into long, yet micrometer-thin cylindrical objects by imparting high diffusion-weighting regimes.
source: Third, it has been shown that dMRI can be made specific to a particular water population restricted into long, yet micrometer-thin cylindrical objects by imparting high diffusion-weighting regimes (McKinnon et al., 2017; Veraart et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: For sufficiently strong diffusion weighting, the power law scaling eventually breaks down, and the dMRI measurement becomes sensitive to the axonal diameter.
source: However, for sufficiently strong diffusion weighting, the power law scaling eventually breaks down, and the dMRI measurement becomes sensitive to the axonal diameter.
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction that is tested experimentally in the study.

claim: Confocal microscopy of the rat corpus callosum validated that the signal arises mainly from the intra-axonal space.
source: Confocal microscopy of the rat corpus callosum (CC) validated that (i) the signal arises mainly from the intra-axonal space, and (ii) the MR-derived axon radius metrics are in good quantitative agreement with those derived from histology.
evidence: This is a validation finding supported by confocal microscopy data.

claim: The MR-derived axon radius metrics are in good quantitative agreement with those derived from histology.
source: Confocal microscopy of the rat corpus callosum (CC) validated that (i) the signal arises mainly from the intra-axonal space, and (ii) the MR-derived axon radius metrics are in good quantitative agreement with those derived from histology.
evidence: This is a validation finding comparing MRI and histology data.

claim: The same signal signatures observed in rodents are observed in living human brain on the Connectom 3T scanner.
source: We then observe the same signal signatures in living human brain on the Connectom 3T scanner, that is, a high performance research scanner with a maximal gradient amplitude of 300 mT/m – a fourfold increase compared to state-of-the art clinical scanners (Glasser et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an observational finding from human MRI data.

claim: The Connectom 3T scanner has a maximal gradient amplitude of 300 mT/m, a fourfold increase compared to state-of-the-art clinical scanners.
source: We then observe the same signal signatures in living human brain on the Connectom 3T scanner, that is, a high performance research scanner with a maximal gradient amplitude of 300 mT/m – a fourfold increase compared to state-of-the art clinical scanners (Glasser et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a technical specification supported by citation.

claim: A consistent residual overestimation of axon radius was observed in MRI compared to histology.
source: Notably, a consistent residual overestimation was observed, whereas the previous simulations (Figure 2) predicted an underestimation.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing MRI and histology data.

claim: Astrocytic processes and cell bodies were found to have volume fractions of about 5% in the genu of the rat corpus callosum.
source: Two notable biological components other than axons were highlighted, namely, astrocytic processes and (neuronal or glial) cell bodies, which were found to have volume fractions of about 5%.
evidence: This is a histological observation from confocal microscopy shown in Figure 5.

claim: The qualitative trends in the axon radius maps are in good agreement with previously reported observations of larger axons in the body of the CC compared to the genu and splenium.
source: Furthermore, the qualitative trends are in good agreement with previously reported observations of larger axons in the body of the CC in comparison to the genu and splenium (Barazany et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an observation from the parameter maps shown in Figure 6, compared to literature.

claim: The exchange model fits the gray matter data better than all other evaluated models in all subjects according to an AIC analysis.
source: The exchange model fits the data better than all other evaluated models in all subjects according to an AIC analysis (data not shown).
evidence: This is a result from AIC analysis of gray matter data.

claim: The tail of the axon radius distribution is typically coarsely sampled in histology, with only a few spikes representing the occasional observation of large axons.
source: Despite a good correspondence of the bulk of axon radii distributions obtained from different histological studies and samples (Aboitiz et al., 1992; Caminiti et al., 2009; Liewald et al., 2014; Tang et al., 1997), the tail of the distribution is typically coarsely sampled, with only a few spikes representing the occasional observation of large axons within the relatively small histological sections, Figure 7.
evidence: This is an observation about histological sampling shown in Figure 7.

claim: For rodent MRI, the precision in the estimation of the effective radius is similar for both MRI and histology modalities.
source: However, for rodent MRI, in which the MRI voxels have the same surface area as the histological patches, the precision in the estimation of the effective radius is similar for both modalities.
evidence: This is a comparison of precision between MRI and histology in rodents.

claim: dMRI provides a precise measurement of the largest axons, which are captured within an MRI voxel.
source: Overall, dMRI provides a precise measurement of the largest axons, which are captured within an MRI voxel.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the capabilities of dMRI.

claim: Histology mainly probes the bulk that consists of smaller axons with high precision.
source: In contrast, histology, so far, mainly probes the bulk that consists of smaller axons with high precision.
evidence: This is a characterization of histological measurements.

claim: Both dMRI and histology modalities are complementary, especially in human MRI for which the voxels are significantly larger than a typical histological sample.
source: Therefore, both modalities are complementary, especially in human MRI for which the voxels are significantly larger than a typical histological sample.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the complementary nature of the two methods.

claim: Several previous studies demonstrated that in vivo dMRI is practically insensitive (< 0.2%) to immobile water signal contributions in the healthy white matter of the living human brain, excluding the cerebellum.
source: Several previous studies, for example Veraart et al. (2019), Tax et al. (2019), and Dhital et al. (2019), demonstrated with various diffusion encoding strategies that in vivo dMRI is practically insensitive, that is < 0.2%, to such signal contributions in the healthy white matter of the living human brain, excluding the cerebellum (Tax et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous studies.

claim: The dot compartment has been observed in fixed brain samples in various studies.
source: In contrast, the dot compartment has been observed in fixed brain samples in various studies (Stanisz et al., 1997; Alexander et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous studies.

claim: Along-axon undulations and curvature might result in an increased apparent radial diffusivity and contribute to an overestimation of the axon radius using dMRI.
source: Third, along-axon undulations (Nilsson et al., 2012) and curvature (Özarslan et al., 2018) might result in an increased apparent radial diffusivity and, as such, contribute to an overestimation of the axon radius using dMRI, especially for increasingly long diffusion times (Lee et al., 2019; Brabec, 2019).
evidence: This is a potential confounding factor, supported by citations.

claim: The effective MR radius in humans was significantly higher than in rats when comparing similar regions of interest.
source: In our study, the effective MR radius in humans was significantly higher than in rats when comparing similar regions of interest, for example the midbody of the CC.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing human and rat MRI data.

claim: Large brains have more large axons and an increased maximal radius, whereas the bulk of axons is not altered.
source: This difference is in agreement with several studies that compared the callosal fiber composition as a function of the brain size of various mammals and concluded that large brains have more large axons and an increased maximal radius, whereas the bulk of axons is not altered (Olivares et al., 2001; Schüz and Preiβl, 1996; Liewald et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on citations to comparative studies across species.

claim: The stick assumption does not hold in the cortical gray matter.
source: Nonetheless, we conclude that the stick assumption does not hold in the cortical GM and that biophysical models building upon that assumption must be interpreted with caution if applied to tissue regions outside of WM.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on gray matter data analysis.

claim: MR-derived effective radii have good quantitative agreement with histology.
source: In summary, we provide a realistic perspective on MR axon radius mapping by showing MR-derived effective radii that have good quantitative agreement with histology.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study.

claim: Clinical applications should focus on pathologies that specifically target larger axons, until other methods are developed that probe the smaller axon diameter.
source: Due to the intrinsic bias of MR-derived axon radii to larger axons, clinical applications should focus on pathologies that specifically target those larger axons, until other methods are developed that probe the smaller axon diameter.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the limitations of the method.

claim: Three Long Evans rats (Female, 12-weeks-old) were transcardially perfused using 4% paraformaldehyde.
source: Three Long Evans rats (Female, 12-weeks-old) were transcardially perfused using 4% paraformaldehyde.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Four healthy volunteers (3 males and 1 female between 22 and 45 years) were recruited for the human study.
source: Four healthy volunteers (3 males and 1 female between 22 and 45 years) were recruited for this study.
evidence: This is a description of the human study participants.

claim: All four human subjects were scanned on a Siemens Connectom 3T MR scanner using a 32-channel receiver coil.
source: All four subjects were scanned on a Siemens Connectom 3T MR scanner using a 32-channel receiver coil.
evidence: This is a description of the MRI scanning setup.
